biological_question: What is the later behavioural outcome that early RFID behaviour is asked to predict, and how is it constructed?
canonical_stage: canonical-endpoint producer (in-repository) + external workbook for the component z-scores only
analysis_resolution: per animal; CombZ has no time resolution
outcome: CombZ = unweighted arithmetic mean of six component z-scores (NOR, sucrose_pref, weight_dev, delta_cort, adrenal_weight, spleen_weight). Direction is NOT harmonised to 'higher = worse': higher CombZ = more resilient-like, lower = worse depressive-like
predictor: not applicable - CombZ is definitional, not estimated
statistical_test: RESOLVED AND CANONICALIZED. Composite: CombZ = unweighted mean of the six component z-scores, ignoring missing components (Excel AVERAGE semantics; 2 of 117 animals have 5 of 6). Verified against the workbook at 2.22e-16. Classification: within Sex, SUS if CombZ < mean(CombZ | CON, same Sex) - populationSD(CombZ | CON, same Sex). Thresholds Male -0.436641698, Female -0.222390844; 0 of 93 label mismatches. Population SD is REQUIRED (sample SD misclassifies 4 animals). Sign conventions: delta_cort, adrenal_weight and spleen_weight are inverted so that higher = more resilient-like for every component.
multiplicity_family: none (no p-value is produced for CombZ itself)
animal_n: 117 animals in the workbook (24 CON, 93 SIS); 111 of them have RFID data and a finite CombZ: CON 24, RES 49, SUS 38; Female 58, Male 53
notes: CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS AUDIT: the z-score reference is WITHIN-SEX control, not '12 male CON' globally. The earlier pass read only the first formula block. Male reference = 12 male CON (batches 1,2,5); female reference = 12 female CON (batches 3,4,6). IRREDUCIBLE EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY: the per-component standardization is written upstream as hard-coded absolute ROW POSITIONS in four per-sex formula blocks, not as a semantic criterion; row ranges and sex only approximately coincide (in organWeight rows 81-118 are mixed-sex but use the male reference), sheets have different row layouts, and sucrosePreference labels four reference animals SIS while every other sheet labels them CON. A single uniform rule does NOT reproduce the shipped values (max deviation ~2.0 even block-aware), so the components are carried through verbatim rather than re-derived, which would change the primary endpoint. Noncanonical alternatives audited and guarded: workbook sheets combZScore and CombZScore_noBatch, plus sus_animals_batchCorrected.csv. See docs/COMBZ_CANONICAL_DEFINITION.md.

biological_question: How broad is the longitudinal RFID behavioural characterization? DECIDED: B3_NOT_JUSTIFIED__USE_FRAMEWORK_SCHEMATIC
canonical_output_file: analysis_ready/pipeline/03_movement_phase_stats/10min/tables/raw_movement_animal_level_endpoints.csv (1221 rows = 111 animals x 11 endpoints; CC1-CC4 x Active/Inactive gives the longitudinal axis)
outcome: mean_movement per animal per cage change per light phase
predictor: none - descriptive framework panel; no contrast is drawn
statistical_test: NONE. Descriptive measurement framework: group medians and interquartile bands only. No contrast, no test, no multiplicity family.
animal_n: 111 animals; only 50 have a complete 72-slot window; per-cell n_ref/n_comp 12-25
notes: DECISION: B3_NOT_JUSTIFIED__USE_FRAMEWORK_SCHEMATIC, adversarially verified. No scientifically clean longitudinal multi-domain overview exists: (i) the canonical analysis_ready/pipeline/ tree contains NO domain-level results table at all; (ii) analysis_ready/output_index.csv records the Stage 14 tree as canonical_path=NA, status='legacy_pending_migration', manuscript_role='exploratory systems layer'; (iii) the registry references only its first_night/10min_based subtree and the release plan stages no sis_domain artifact among its 45; (iv) the strict-completeness defect PROVABLY bites - OQ755/CC2, OQ770/CC1 and OQ771/CC1 carry finite domain scores computed from 2-of-3, 4-of-5 and 2-of-3 contributors, i.e. three named animals scored on a different formula from their peers, which Functions/first_night_domain_helpers.R:21-24 explicitly forbids; (v) every HMM/latent-state domain and every inactive-rest/circadian reading is barred by docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md items 1-3. Panel B is therefore a descriptive framework grounded in the one registry-cleared longitudinal construct. Source choice is EXPLICIT configuration (PANEL_B_SOURCE), not file availability. B1 and B2 remain available as candidates/Extended Data.

biological_question: Alternative, genuinely longitudinal and broader domain map, reported because Panel B has two live candidates and neither may be chosen silently
canonical_input_file: analysis_ready/03_derived_metrics/5min_based/all_behavior_metrics.csv plus the Stage 08 HMM occupancy bundle at 10min_based
analysis_resolution: MIXED AND MISLABELLED: the file's own resolution column reads 10min_based for all 84 rows, but that describes only the HMM contributor; six of the seven domains come from the 5min_based backbone
outcome: DomainScore per animal per cage change per phase
predictor: Group interacted with Sex, adjusted for factor(CageChangeIndex), animal random intercept
statistical_test: lmerTest::lmer(DomainScore ~ Group * Sex + factor(CageChangeIndex) + (1 | AnimalNum)) with emmeans contrasts within Sex; Hedges g computed separately on one mean per animal
animal_n: 111 animals; 444 animal-epoch rows per domain and phase (441 for the HMM domain and for social spatial organisation)
notes: 84 rows = 7 domains x Active/Inactive x 2 Sex x 3 contrasts, so it is the ONLY artifact that can fill a broad one-row-per-domain heatmap with a phase axis. Four reasons it is not simply adopted: it appears in NO registry row and in NO release plan entry; it still displays the HMM-derived 'Behavioral state architecture' domain, which the first-night contract removed entirely; ALL 8 of its FDR-supported cells are in the Inactive phase, which docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md item 3 forbids interpreting as biology; and its domain scores are built with na.rm = TRUE plus coalesce(missing, 0), so an animal missing a contributor is scored on a different formula from its peers - a practice Functions/first_night_domain_helpers.R:21-24 explicitly rejects. It also ships no confidence intervals. Built here as an extended-data candidate only

biological_question: What does locomotor behaviour look like across animals during the first active phase after the first cage change, and does it separate the later phenotype groups?
canonical_output_file: analysis_ready/pipeline/09_early_prediction/10min/tables/model_ladder_input.csv (111 rows, one per animal; the exact frame every Stage 09 statistic runs on: features plus the CombZ outcome). Its outcome-free twin is early_behavior_features_wide.csv. Window identity: early_window_contract_summary.csv. Descriptive contrasts: primary_feature_group_contrasts_descriptive.csv. Pooled group summary: primary_feature_group_summary.csv
outcome: Movement_mean = animal-level arithmetic mean of per-bin Movement, where per-bin Movement is the COUNT of RFID position transitions in that 10-min bin. So the unit is mean transitions per 10-min bin, NOT a total. Observed animal range 0.944 to 7.310; group means CON 3.788, RES 3.388, SUS 4.008
statistical_test: THREE COMPETING IMPLEMENTATIONS THAT DISAGREE IN VERDICT. (1) Stage 09: wilcox.test on animal-level Movement_mean, POOLED across sex, three planned pairs, BH within feature; SUS-RES p = 0.00749, q = 0.0225, effect r = 0.287 - but the filename and the ReportingRole column both say DESCRIPTIVE, and no CI is emitted. (2) Stage 20 (the DECLARED canonical categorical contrast, identical window): bin-level GAMM within sex, log1p(Movement) ~ Batch + Group + smooths + animal random effect, mgcv::bam with AR1, Wald on the window-average and window-integrated AUC; ALL SIX CONTRASTS NULL, min BH q = 0.796. (3) Stage 14: lm(Movement_mean z-scored within sex ~ Group * Sex) + emmeans; Female SUS-RES q = 0.0856, null
multiplicity_family: Stage 09 descriptive: BH within feature, 3 contrasts, family not named in the file. Stage 20 declared canonical: PRIMARY_FIRST_ACTIVE__2Sex_x_3GroupContrasts, 6 tests, BH
animal_n: 111 animals; Female CON 12 / RES 24 / SUS 22, Male CON 12 / RES 25 / SUS 16; 7879 of 7992 target slots observed; 50 animals complete, 61 missing leading slots only, 0 interior and 0 trailing gaps
notes: The WINDOW is unambiguous and parity-tested: first Active phase block after CC1, fixed clock 18:30 inclusive to 06:30 exclusive, exactly 12 h, all UTC; Functions/first_night_window_helpers.R is a byte-parity-tested re-implementation and Testing/tests/test_first_night_window_parity.R asserts row-for-row identity with Stage 09 at both resolutions. Movement_mean agrees to full double precision across all three producers. The ambiguity is purely INFERENTIAL, and it is consequential: the only nominally significant categorical result is the one the repo labels non-claimable, while the declared canonical contrast is entirely null. Panel C therefore displays the DISTRIBUTION only and annotates no categorical effect. Two traps: early_observation_hours and early_observed_bins in the Stage 09 and Stage 16 animal tables describe the whole ~48 h CC1 Active epoch, NOT the 12 h window, so they must never be quoted as window coverage; and ten stale first_night_*.csv files from a superseded Stage 20 run still sit beside the current first_active_*.csv files

biological_question: Does early locomotor magnitude relate continuously to the later behavioural outcome, rather than only through the phenotype dichotomy?
canonical_input_file: analysis_ready/pipeline/09_early_prediction/10min/tables/model_ladder_input.csv (111 rows: Movement_mean and the CombZ outcome per animal)
statistical_test: Spearman rank correlation with a 5000-iteration animal-resampling bootstrap CI, POOLED across sex. Movement_mean vs CombZ: rho = -0.3903, 95 percent CI [-0.5474, -0.2092], p = 2.293e-05, BH q = 6.878e-05, n = 111. NOT ordinary least squares, so no least-squares line may be drawn
multiplicity_family: Three canonical primary feature associations, BH (spearman_p_bh)
notes: The canonical framing is POOLED across sex, not sex-facetted: the formal feature-by-Sex interaction is null for all three features (all q = 0.895) and the repo states that sex-stratified estimates are descriptive and are NOT interaction tests. The panel is therefore drawn pooled, with the later outcome group carried redundantly by point shape and fill (sex is not encoded); a sex-facetted version is exported as a clearly-labelled descriptive candidate only. Because the inferential model is rank-based, the panel shows the raw scatter plus a descriptive quantile-bin trend, and a rank-space companion whose reference line has slope exactly equal to the canonical rho. The other two features of the same a priori family must travel with it: Movement_rmssd is FDR-supported but must not be called an independent predictor, and Entropy_acf1 is NOT FDR-supported at the primary resolution (q = 0.0667)

biological_question: Does first-night behaviour carry information about the later outcome that generalises to animals the model never saw?
producer_script: Analysis/09_early_prediction_model_ladder.R (loo_lm_predict at :383-418; run_primary_outcome_permutation at :1605-1626; fixed registry at :1635-1669)
outcome: CONTINUOUS CombZ. There is NO classification model anywhere in Stage 09: no logistic fit, no ROC, no AUC. Group is excluded from every primary model
predictor: Headline model: Movement_mean alone. Supporting model: Movement_mean + Movement_rmssd + Entropy_acf1. Two sex-adjusted variants are declared sensitivities with no permutation test
statistical_test: Exhaustive leave-one-animal-out ordinary least squares: each animal in turn is removed, the model is refitted on the remaining 110 and predicts the held-out animal, with training-fold-only median imputation. Metric cv_r2_vs_mean: headline LOAO out-of-sample R2 = 0.15939, supporting model 0.15245, intercept-only baseline -0.01826. Reference: 1000 full-refit outcome permutations, seed 20260811, which reshuffle CombZ and re-run the entire LOAO loop; empirical p = (1 + count) / 1001 = 1/1001 for both non-null models. Null summary: median -0.0313, 2.5-97.5 percent quantiles [-0.0442, 0.0059]. Companion robustness: 100 repeats of grouped 5-fold CV, seed 521, mean R2 0.15582, split-to-split 2.5-97.5 percent quantiles [0.1159, 0.1790]
multiplicity_family: None. adjustment_method is recorded as 'None; empirical full-refit outcome permutation' and multiplicity_family as 'Model-specific full-refit outcome permutation'
animal_n: 111 animals; 222 held-out prediction rows = 111 animals x 2 fixed models
